data.narrative:
Chaos Industries, a Series D defense and security company founded by John Tenet, Bo Marr, Brett Cummings, and Gavin Hood, carries a current post-money valuation of $4.5B following $1B+ in total capital raised. The peer set comprises 10 comparable companies across Defense & Security—2 public (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS) and 8 private, including Helsing, Saronic, Onebrief, Anduril Industries, and Shield AI.

Two valuation methods were applied to triangulate fair value. Stage-progression analysis, using a 1.5x multiplier typical of Series D advancement, yields $6.8B from the $4.5B base. Peer-median valuation across three same-sector, same-stage comparables—Helsing ($18.0B), Saronic ($9.2B), and Onebrief ($2.1B)—produces a median of $9.2B, with a range spanning $2.1B to $18.0B.

These methods support a triangulated valuation range of $5.7B to $10.6B, with a midpoint of $8.0B. This implies 33–78% upside from the current $4.5B valuation. The wide peer dispersion ($2.1B–$18.0B) reflects material uncertainty around stage-appropriate multiples in defense tech, likely driven by variable commercial traction and differentiation in AI/autonomy capabilities. Further diligence on revenue run-rate, contract pipeline, and competitive positioning would narrow this range materially.
